first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, so simplifying onboarding is the most directly aligned intervention and avoids the known 30-day retention risk of promotional pricing. Verify the archived onboarding and activation records before committing, while testing cautiously because improved early activation may not automatically translate into sustainable qualified revenue.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding, prioritizing the directly observed 4% completion decline while also addressing the 6% activation decline. The verified record showed a 13% completion lift, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and 3% higher 30-day retention, making this the strongest sustainable option. Activation messaging is also validated, but onboarding has the broader completion and retention impact. Measure qualified revenue, activation, completion, time-to-value, and retention; do not assume early gains automatically translate to long-term revenue.

final2.rationale: Respond to the sharply increased price-sensitive SMB churn with a tightly targeted, time-limited offer rather than a broad price cut. Prior evidence indicates promotional pricing can lift acquisition and revenue but materially harms 30-day retention, so gate eligibility, cap discount depth and duration, and continue only if qualified revenue and retention remain acceptable. This is a defensive test, not a change to the sustainable growth strategy.
